blind.table_distance_name: gothic stained glass window wall section
blind.description: A vertical section of a dressed-stone masonry wall containing an arched Gothic lancet window. The masonry consists of neatly stacked, beveled rectangular stone blocks painted in cool grey-blue with subtle edge highlights and slight mossy/warm tinting at the base. The window frame is a pointed arch with molded stone trim, a projecting stone windowsill, a central stone mullion column, and a small circular tracery opening at the top. Set within the stone frame is a stained glass panel featuring diamond/lozenge patterns in warm amber, red, orange, and olive tones with subtle glowing or light-catching edges. All geometry is solid, clean, and continuous with stylized hand-painted textures.
blind.from_above: From straight above, it appears as a thick, rectangular block of wall composed of five visible top blocks, with the window frame and sill projecting slightly outward from both broad faces.
blind.height_vs_figure: Roughly 1.1 times the height of the 5 ft 9 in figure (around 6.3 ft tall), and about 0.7 times as wide as it is tall (around 4.2 ft wide).
